actions.incomplete: Try the five small activities first

page1.title: A flashlight for a long story
page1.subtitle: The model can only use a limited part of the text at one time.
page1.question: Can the model see the whole story?
page1.intro: A story can be very long. The model needs a smaller reading space for the text it is using right now.
page1.analogy: Imagine reading in the dark with a flashlight. You can use the words inside the light, while the rest are harder to reach.
page1.takeaway: The model works with a limited view of the text, not an unlimited view of everything ever written.
page1.bridge: Now give this limited reading space its technical name: the Context Window.

page2.title: Meet the context window
page2.subtitle: The window marks which tokens are available right now.
page2.question: What is a context window?
page2.intro: The text is already split into tokens. A boundary around some of those tokens shows the model's current reading space.
page2.inside: The model can use these tokens now
page2.outside: These tokens are outside this view
page2.definition: The group of tokens available to the model while it works on the next part of the text.
page2.takeaway: Context means the text available to the model right now.
page2.bridge: But text keeps growing. What happens when a new token arrives?

page3.title: The window moves
page3.subtitle: New tokens enter while older tokens can move out of view.
page3.question: What happens when the story gets longer?
page3.intro: Add tokens one at a time. Keep watching the same five-token window.
page3.waiting: Add a token and watch the window move.
page3.moved: A new token entered. An older token moved outside the window.
page3.finished: The story grew, but the reading space stayed limited.
page3.analogy: When the board is full, adding something new may mean an older note is no longer visible.
page3.takeaway: As text grows, the model's available window moves with it.
page3.bridge: When an older clue leaves the window, can it still help the current calculation?

page4.title: Outside means unavailable
page4.subtitle: A useful clue cannot help if it is outside the current window.
page4.question: Can the model use a clue it cannot see?
page4.intro: The word “bank” can have different meanings. The useful word “river” has moved outside the current window.
page4.quizInstruction: Use the context window to answer one question.
page4.answerChecked: Answer checked — read the feedback below
page4.ask: Which text can the model use right now?
page4.optionInside: “They sat on the bank” — inside the window
page4.correct: Yes. It can use the visible sentence, but without “river” the meaning of “bank” may still be unclear.
page4.tryAgain: That clue would be useful, but it is outside the model's current view.
page4.takeaway: Words outside the context window cannot directly help with the current step.
page4.bridge: A larger window can keep more clues in view—but is it unlimited?

page5.title: Bigger is still limited
page5.subtitle: A larger context window holds more tokens, but it still has an edge.
page5.question: Does a bigger window remember everything?
page5.intro: Move the control to give the model a larger reading window. Count what stays visible and what remains outside.
page5.explanation: Real models can have much larger context windows than this teaching picture. They are still limited, and this is not human memory.
page5.takeaway: A bigger context window provides more text, not unlimited memory or understanding.
page5.bridge: Put the moving, limited Context Window into one complete reading journey.

page6.title: Your context discovery
page6.subtitle: Connect the idea before moving to helpful clues.
page6.question: What did the model have available?
page6.intro: Follow the reading journey from a long story to the tokens available right now.
page6.step1Note: The story may contain many tokens.
page6.step2Note: A limited reading space moves through them.
page6.step3Note: Only the tokens in view can help now.
page6.point1: The model does not have an unlimited view of all text.
page6.point2: Its context window contains the tokens available right now.
page6.point3: When text grows, older tokens can move outside that window.
page6.next: Inside the window, some tokens are more helpful than others. Next, we will shine a spotlight on those clues.
